basis: This audit covers changes in the current fix round after the pre-pressure commit 926a3524a (15:11 UTC). Functional failures and controlled-clock regressions are separate from timing measured under deliberate host stress.

changes.change: Gentler easing and a clock released after the inverse paint
changes.evidence: The easing curve travels 38 percent in 17 ms independent of host load; the paused-inverse regression verifies paint before clock release.

changes.change: Real-node FLIP with batched reads and temporary layers
changes.evidence: Implements the requested transform-only layout contract and removes redundant staged wrapping machinery.

changes.change: Native grid prelude, per-column handover and additional activation phase
changes.evidence: Introduced to move frame-time numbers under host pressure; the final implementation uses one destination read and inverse release.

changes.change: Additional containment tuning, nine-keyframe counters, two-node batches and 600 ms warm lead
changes.evidence: No quiet-machine causal performance evidence for the new tuning. Reverted the new card/frame/text-group containment rules and restored the pre-pressure settings: 13 keyframes, four-node batches and 150 ms warm lead. Existing pre-pressure board/column/body containment remains.

changes.change: Committed native inverse ownership through release
changes.evidence: Controlled RAF regression: canceling pointer warm-up must retain an already committed paused inverse until release; removing its active ownership cancels the effects.

changes.change: Idle watchdog cancellation of an authorized width control
changes.evidence: Controlled RAF and elapsed-time regression: the width button must still commit after the idle preparation deadline. Removing the fix drops the update.

changes.change: Latest width control owns its promotion queue
changes.evidence: The previous implementation commits an older longer queue after a later control; the public regression preserves the latest choice.

changes.change: Warmed source origins and live-content invalidation
changes.evidence: Moving an ancestor by 40 pixels before commit produced a spurious inverse offset; the public regression requires zero offset. New or changed cards refresh their source.

changes.change: Retarget glyph anchors and form-safe neutral groups
changes.evidence: Retargets preserve leading glyph positions at natural font size. Native forms cannot host a ShadowRoot; shared browser coverage checks usable task forms during width changes.

changes.change: Header mutation ownership and stable Board measurement/rendering
changes.evidence: Header controls from the width commit must not trigger a second FLIP; card measurement waits for the layout-end event and width-only changes render no cards.
Prevents transformed content from creating horizontal scroll displacement; shared scroll/reader cases cover the behavior.

changes.change: Retarget at the same painted width but different natural wrapping
changes.evidence: On a quiet host, the shared rapid-retarget case failed with a 6.684 pixel glyph jump. Including changed natural widths in the FLIP fixes all five phases; both scroll and retarget cases pass with 1491 assertions.

changes.change: Reader reveal before an asynchronous navigation scroll event
changes.evidence: The keyboard browser case failed twice on a quiet host: an inverse returned the revealed reader offscreen. Navigation now retires its pending inverse when React already changed the scroll position; the existing browser case and a controlled DOM regression pass without an additional RAF phase.

changes.change: Warm source retained before promotion completion
changes.evidence: Two quiet-host activation stalls of 66.6 and 66.7 ms reproduced. A controlled regression showed three card-rect reads when the commit overtook promotion, instead of the required source/destination pair. Retaining the initial source removes the duplicate read and two trailing warm-up RAFs. The 150 ms lead, four-node batches and 13 keyframes are unchanged.
